issue.title: plugin host: every auto-update restart (syscall.Exec) leaves the old Bun host a zombie
issue.body:
**What happens**

magpie 0.1.1322 on Linux, run under systemd as

```
magpie web --addr 0.0.0.0:3430 --no-open --gateway
```

with `{"autoRestart": true, "updateEvery": 30}` in settings.json. The service has been up two days and `ps` shows **27 `<defunct>` `magpie-bun` children** of the magpie PID, never reaped, a new one at every update:

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,lstart,stat,cmd | grep -E 'magpie-bun|magpie web'
   1605       1  Tue Oct 20 03:47:22 2026  Ssl  /home/<user>/.local/bin/magpie web --addr 0.0.0.0:3430 --no-open --gateway
   4640    1605  Tue Oct 20 05:11:50 2026  Z    [magpie-bun] <defunct>
  24225    1605  Tue Oct 20 11:16:16 2026  Z    [magpie-bun] <defunct>
  28306    1605  Tue Oct 20 12:46:00 2026  Z    [magpie-bun] <defunct>
  ... 24 more ...
 121500    1605  Thu Oct 22 12:20:46 2026  Z    [magpie-bun] <defunct>
 126013    1605  Thu Oct 22 14:22:19 2026  Sl   /home/<user>/.cache/magpie/bun/1.4.3/magpie-bun run /home/<user>/.cache/magpie/plugin-host/host-05ed1f913c11.js
```

Each zombie's start time is exactly a `● magpie web on http://…` line in the journal, i.e. the Bun host a given version started; the journal of three updates in 90 minutes reads

```
11:20:54  ● magpie web on …   → zombie 119530
11:50:33  ● magpie web on …   → zombie 120511
12:20:46  ● magpie web on …   → zombie 121500
```

(the binary's mtime follows the same lines — same PID 1605 the whole time). The cost today is nil — RSS 0, `Tasks: 45` of 1016, `pid_max` 4194304 — but it never stops: updating every 30 minutes leaves ~48 a day for as long as the service runs.

**Why, as far as I can tell**

`gui.Web.Wait()` restarts into the new version with `syscall.Exec` (`internal/update/proc_unix.go`), keeping the PID — which is what keeps the service manager and the open page happy. Before exec it calls `proc.EndProbes()`, on the principle stated there that "magpie is exiting or putting a new version in its place, and nothing would end them after" — but the same is not done for the plugin host.

The Bun host outlives the exec, and the new image has no `host` for it: the `cmd.Wait()` that reaps it lives in `host.read()` (`internal/plugin/host.go`), and that goroutine went away with the old image. When the child finally exits — its stdin is a CLOEXEC pipe, so it gets EOF with the exec — nothing calls `Wait` on it, and it stays `<defunct>` under the same PID.

I checked that the other stop path is fine: changing the plugin list (`touch plugins.json` + a gateway request) retires the host and it is reaped properly — the old `magpie-bun` PID disappears and the zombie count does not change. It is specifically the reexec path.

**Suggested fix**

In `gui.Web.Wait()`, before `update.Reexec`, stop the plugin host and wait for it to be gone — the way `plugin.Settle` does (`plugin.Restart()` then wait for `retiring`) — so nothing of the old image's children outlives the exec, same as `EndProbes` for probes.

**Environment**

- magpie 0.1.1322, Linux x86_64 (glibc), Bun 1.4.3
- `magpie web --gateway` under systemd, `autoRestart: true`, `updateEvery: 30`
- plugins from @magpie-community/* (7 listed, one updated by the host during the same window)

comments.body:
I reproduced this with a real Bun host and a real Linux `exec`, and put a fix in my fork: [863a1e72](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/863a1e725073a19829e8986e92c92c20a48e6003) (branch `fix/reexec-plugin-host`; its follow-up only lets the parent test clean up fixtures).

`Web.Wait` now drains the gateway, then calls `plugin.Settle` before reexec. Draining matters because gateway requests/background work could otherwise start another host during shutdown. The host's stop path also waits for `cmd.Wait` to finish, including after a forced kill. Its existing renewal grace period is retained.

The Linux regression runs the test binary again in the same PID and uses `wait4` to check that the old host has already been reaped. The original code failed. Calling `Settle` alone still failed the forced-kill case 3/3; waiting for reaping fixes both normal and forced exits. Related shutdown, renewal, pipe-failure and stream tests passed with `-race -count=3`.

No production service or vendor account was touched. macOS/Windows runtime and an actual downloaded auto-update were not exercised. This covers reexec, not the separate SIGTERM/SIGINT work in #1258.

Combined validation: these changes are included in [065f0c8f](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/065f0c8ffc9e30225f3d468ef41ec414aab75e02) on `fix/issue-batch-20261023`. At that exact commit, `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m`, native/Linux/Windows vet and native/Linux/Windows builds all passed with Go 1.26.8, a temporary HOME and pinned Go caches (Linux host, umask 027). Cross-platform builds/vet are not Windows runtime tests. These full-suite results apply to the combined commit; the focused results above apply to the individual fix.

Same on a second machine, and still there at `main` (`59fdab0af`): `internal/update/proc_unix.go` and `gui.Web.Wait()` are unchanged since the build that shows it.

**Environment:** magpie `v0.1.2629` (`79f8379`, 2026-11-01, an ancestor of `59fdab0af`), Linux x86_64 in a container, `magpie serve --web=0.0.0.0:7331 --no-open` as PID 9, `"autoRestart": true`, rebuilt often over two days.

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,comm | grep 'magpie-bun'
   314       9 Z    magpie-bun
  2167       9 Z    magpie-bun
  2967       9 Z    magpie-bun
  ...                                   (22 in all)
231388       9 Sl   magpie-bun          <- the host of the image now running

$ ps -eo stat,comm | grep -c Z
22
$ awk '/magpie gateway on/{n++} END{print n}' ~/.local/share/magpie/web.log
23
```

23 images have run under that one PID and 22 Bun hosts are `<defunct>`: exactly one per reexec, none missed, none duplicated. Each zombie's start time is the host that was up when the previous image was replaced — 21:33:47 → reexec 21:59, 22:00:47 → 22:19, 22:19:55 → 23:01, 23:02:05 → 23:09, 02:10:38 → 05:10 — and each new image wrote a new `plugin-host/host-<hash>.js` (five of those on disk).

Two things that may help whoever fixes it:

`/proc/<pid>/exe` is the binary now on disk (`md5sum` equal to `.local/bin/magpie`, mtime 23:29) while the process started two days earlier, which is what pins this on the in-place exec rather than on a handover.

After the exec the parent holds no pipes at all — `/proc/9/fd` has exactly three, the live host's stdin/stdout/stderr — because they are all `O_CLOEXEC` and the exec closed them. That is also why the old host is not stuck: it gets stdin EOF and exits. There is just no `wait4` left to take it, since the only one was `host.read()`'s `cmd.Wait()` in the image that was replaced.

And since a reexec is the one place magpie puts a new image in its own PID, the ending should probably be the general one: anything else that outlives an exec is the same `<defunct>` under the same PID afterwards (pii's helper, whatever `magpie awake` holds — #4188's `caffeinate` is that shape too, though it may not be this path). The `plugin.Settle` plus wait-for-reap in skygunner's comment above is the shape I would expect; it is not in `59fdab0af` yet.

Thank you for the second machine and the forensics — the `O_CLOEXEC` reading (the exec closes every pipe, so the old host dies of stdin EOF with no `wait4` left to reap it) is exactly the mechanism the fix runs on: [fix/reexec-plugin-host](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/reexec-plugin-host) (`863a1e72`) drains the gateway, then `plugin.Settle`, then waits for the reaping before the reexec, covering both the clean and the forced-kill exit. Still awaiting pickup — nothing in `59fdab0af` takes it, as you found. Your broader point is noted: anything else that outlives the exec under the same PID is the same `<defunct>` shape afterwards; the branch scopes itself to the reexec path for now.

Follow-up: the reexec plugin-host fix has now landed upstream as f4c664a09ca0e2dcdab3d41290e10ba440a1367f: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/f4c664a09ca0e2dcdab3d41290e10ba440a1367f . On main at b1e8eb15, Web.Wait calls plugin.EndHosts immediately before update.Reexec; EndHosts prevents new hosts, stops live and retiring hosts, and waits for each child to be reaped. This supersedes my earlier "still awaiting pickup" status for this plugin-host path.

I reran TestEndHostsLeavesNoChild on Linux at that baseline with the related web/plugin tests: it passed. I did not perform a downloaded-update reexec against a deployed service, and this does not establish that unrelated helper processes in #4188 are fixed.

The separate SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful-drain port discussed in #1258 is refreshed on the same baseline in https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/1258-web-shutdown-current (e094d775c13ac24014d0227365d00df9e7c487b6, with the original author's co-author credit). It preserves ignored signals and SIGHUP behavior, covers web and serve --web, drains held real HTTP requests before exit, and suppresses an update restart on cancellation. Twelve Linux subprocess scenarios, the ignored-signal disposition check, race, related tests, vet and nogui build passed. This branch uses upstream's EndHosts rather than carrying a second implementation. Native Windows/macOS and a real update download were not exercised. The upstream PR has not been modified.

issue.title: fix(web): exit cleanly on SIGTERM and SIGINT

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body: ## Problem and reproduction During Railway image auto-updates, the old `magpie web` deployment was marked `CRASHED` immediately after `Stopping Container`, while the replacement deployment became `SUCCESS` seconds later. This generated misleading crash notifications for planned stops. Reproduced the process exit behavior locally using the exact released Linux/amd64 image, `magpie v0.1.1110`: `ghcr.io/yetone/magpie@sha256:15da0cb01bba31bf645ca0513b0f9524609e780c0b98f8bec6b5a0bc30670d60` The container ran `exec /magpie web --addr 0.0.0.0:3430 --no-open` with isolated disposable configuration and no external network access. Both the authenticated web page and `/magpie healthcheck` worked before stopping it. | Stop operation | Released binary | Fixed binary in the same image | | --- | --- | --- | | `docker stop --signal SIGTERM --timeout 10` | exit 2 | exit 0 | | `docker stop --signal SIGINT --timeout 10` | exit 2 | exit 0 | | `POST /api/window/quit` | exit 0 | exit 0 | All stops finished in under one second; none was OOM-killed or reached Docker's kill timeout. These are local Linux container results (Docker on macOS arm64, running linux/amd64), not a redeployment or end-to-end notification test on Railway. ## Behavior change The global `endProbesOnSignal` handler terminated `magpie web` on SIGINT/SIGTERM while `Web.Wait` only waited for the page's Quit action. Web now owns those two signals using the existing `ownSignals` handoff, as the desktop app and TUI already do. `webCmd` passes cancellation to `Web.Wait`. It closes the page listener, drains this process's gateway using the existing `stopServing` path and deadline, then returns to main for probe and session cleanup with a successful exit. SIGHUP retains its existing termination behavior. The page's Quit and restart-to-update also drain the gateway; a stop signal suppresses reexec, while a page-requested update keeps the existing arguments and run key. See the updated [GUI app shell shutdown contract](https://github.com/AmAzing129/magpie/blob/fix/web-signal-shutdown/docs/subsystems/gui-shell.md#browser-mode-shutdown), [`web_cli.go`](https://github.com/AmAzing129/magpie/blob/fix/web-signal-shutdown/web_cli.go), and [`internal/gui/web.go`](https://github.com/AmAzing129/magpie/blob/fix/web-signal-shutdown/internal/gui/web.go). This does not implement the independent-worker update handover discussed in #577, change Railway configuration, or disable crash notifications. ## Verification - Added `TestWebShutdown`, which runs the actual `main` entry point in isolated subprocesses and checks SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP and authenticated page Quit. - Before the fix, SIGTERM failed with `signal: terminated` and SIGINT with `signal: interrupt`; SIGHUP and page Quit controls passed. After the fix, all four pass. - The new regression plus the existing global signal tests passed with `-race -count=20`. - `go vet ./...`, native macOS `go build`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -tags nogui`, and `GOOS=windows go build` passed. Windows was cross-compiled, not runtime-tested. - Local container comparison above passed against the released and fixed binaries. Temporary containers and their configuration were removed; no production credentials or services were used. - Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` passed with Go 1.26.8 and the real Bun 1.4.2 executable on PATH, with an isolated HOME and pinned Go caches. The first run used a mise Bun shim / Bun 1.3.14 and failed three plugin tests; using the runtime required by CI resolved those failures without changing plugin code. - No UI assets or appearance changed; no visual/UI suite was run. --- ### 🎬 界面预览 CI 用这个 PR 的代码构建并真实运行 magpie（沙盒环境，配置了真实的 DeepSeek key），按改动自动操作、截图和录屏 · 5a88cdc · [运行记录](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/actions/runs/37737544241) **改动**（按代码）：该 PR 只改 `magpie web` 的进程信号处理：SIGINT/SIGTERM 由 web 自己接管，关闭页面服务并排空网关后正常退出，SIGHUP 与页面「退出」行为不变；没有任何页面、样式、文案或交互的改变。 看了改动，没有找到用户能看到的界面变化，所以没有录制。详见[运行记录](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/actions/runs/37737544241)。

issue.title: Windows: the app (and its gateway) disappears mid-stream under load and never comes back

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
# Windows: the app (and its gateway) disappears mid-stream under load and never comes back — no record left

## What happened

On Windows 11 (10.0.26200), magpie was serving the local gateway at `127.0.0.1:3425` for about 20 `pi` sessions doing long streaming requests. At **2026-10-23 00:36:37 (local, UTC+8)** the app was simply gone: the port stopped answering in the middle of several streams, every client got `Connection error`, and no new magpie process appeared. The gateway stayed down for ~50 minutes until I ran `magpie tray`; the first request then completed at 01:26:47 and everything has been fine since.

There is no crash record of any kind on this machine, and I could not reproduce it on demand, so I am reporting what is reproducible from the logs and asking what would be the best way to capture the next one.

## Timeline (local, UTC+8)

| time | what |
|---|---|
| 10-22 21:55:03 | a sibling `magpie web` (0.1.1322) logs that the gateway on 3425 is served by another magpie **0.1.1318** |
| 23:00–00:36 | gateway handled 2,550 requests for ~20 pi sessions, peak 37 concurrent streams (00:20:01); largest request 325k input tokens |
| 00:35:54.5 | last request the gateway completed (`200`) |
| 00:36:23–00:36:36.9 | 12 `%TEMP%\magpie-conversation-*` files take their last write; nothing after that |
| **00:36:37** | pi clients: `terminated`, then `Connection error.` (00:36:39, :43, :51, 00:37:21–35) |
| 01:25:12–26 | still `Connection error.` (no gateway at all) |
| ~01:26 | `magpie tray` started; first completed request 01:26:47 |

## Evidence that this was the whole process ending, not a request error

- Clients were cut mid-stream at the same instant (above), not with a 5xx.
- The gateway's own usage log (`~/.config/magpie/usage.jsonl`) has all `200`s up to 00:35:54.5 — 190 records in 00:30–00:40, no `5xx`, no `499` — and then nothing until after the restart.
- 12 in-flight conversation temp files stop being written within the same ~14 s window and are left behind (the next one is at 12:22); a normal shutdown would not leave the in-flight set like that.
- `127.0.0.1:3425` stayed closed for the whole 50 minutes (clients still failing at 01:25).

Note: the two `magpie.exe mcp image` processes that stayed alive are children of the pi sessions (PPIDs are pi), not of the app, so they say nothing either way about the app's exit.

## Why there is no crash record (on this machine)

- Windows Error Reporting is **disabled system-wide** here: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting` has `Disabled=1`, `LoggingDisabled=1`. `ReportArchive`/`ReportQueue` are empty and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps` has no magpie dump.
- The Application log has **no** 1000 (Application Error), 1001 (WER), 1002 (Application Hang) or .NET Runtime events in the whole 24 h around the incident; nothing mentioning magpie at all. (Expected with WER off, and a Go panic/OOM writes no such event anyway.)
- magpie keeps no run/crash log that I can find: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\magpie` only has `market\`, `~/.config/magpie` has no `logs/` or `*crash*`, and `magpie --help` has no `log`/`doctor`/`version` command — only `magpie heap`/`magpie cpu` for a live process.
- The app is normally started from its Start Menu shortcut (`Magpie.lnk`), so there is no console for a panic trace to go to.

## What it is not

No system cause: no Kernel-Power 41/42/107/109/131, no Power-Troubleshooter, no 6008/1074/6005/6006, no Resource-Exhaustion-Detector 2004, no Defender events, no reboot (`LastBootUpTime` 2026-10-20 14:03:23); the machine and the other processes kept running. The upstream disconnects around 23:27 and later are separate — the gateway was alive and serving around them.

## Update settings (could not confirm or rule out an update restart)

`settings.json` has `"updateEvery": 30` and `"autoRestart": true` (UI: *Restart automatically — once an update is downloaded, restarts into it when no agent request is in flight*). New releases existed at the time (0.1.1323 at 23:03, 0.1.1324 at 23:36 local), **but nothing was installed at 00:36**: the exe's birth/mtime did not change, `last-version` was not written then, and no `.new` file was left. The current exe was installed at 12:10 today (0.1.1330). So I can neither prove an update restart nor exclude a relaunch handshake that failed.

One oddity that may be related to the update history: the instance serving the gateway reported **0.1.1318**, while the binary on disk (`C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\文件\magpie.exe`) was **0.1.1313** (birth 2026-10-22 00:15), and a `magpie web` started at 21:54 was 0.1.1322. So this machine had been running a build newer than its installed exe.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200, 31.3 GB RAM.
- magpie: gateway instance 0.1.1318 at the time (see above); installed exe 0.1.1313; now 0.1.1330 (updated 2026-10-23 12:10).
- Gateway `127.0.0.1:3425`; ~20 `pi` sessions, long streams; 2,550 requests in 96 minutes, peak 37 concurrent.

## Possible conditions

- ~20 clients on long-lived streams, 30–40 requests/min sustained for hours, peak 37 in flight, single requests up to 325k input tokens.
- It happened about 4.5 h into that session (the gateway had been serving since at least 21:55), with no error trend before it.
- Auto-update on with 30-minute checks, and a newer release was available at the time (but nothing was installed then).

## What I am asking

1. Is there a way to get a panic/exit record on Windows in this setup? Would a console `magpie serve` run (or redirecting stderr) be the recommended way to catch it next time, or is there a debug/log flag I missed?
2. Any known issue with the gateway dying under many concurrent long streams / large contexts (memory), or with the app exiting instead of restarting on an update?
3. Related issues I found while checking: #2362 (macOS Update and Restart exits without relaunching), #2272 (Windows first install of an update fails), #3285 (auto-update reexec path), #2932 (panic kills the app), #2278 / #3318 (main-process memory growth).

issue.title: macOS: every keep-awake session leaves a zombie caffeinate child under the magpie process

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happens

On macOS (arm64, Apple Silicon), every time magpie starts a "keep awake" session while an agent is running, it spawns `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w <magpie_pid>`. When the session ends, `caffeinate` exits but magpie never reaps it, so every session leaves one `<defunct>` (zombie) child under the magpie PID.

After three days of normal use (magpie 0.1.1985, running as a menu-bar app via `magpie serve --web=127.0.0.1:3430`), the magpie process has 12 zombie children plus 7 live `caffeinate` children and 1 live plugin-host Bun worker:

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,lstart,command | awk '$2==8525'
  2821  8525 S    Tue Oct 27 08:49:50 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
  6464  8525 Z    Tue Oct 27 16:38:30 2026     <defunct>
  7934  8525 Z    Tue Oct 27 12:01:00 2026     <defunct>
  8195  8525 S    Tue Oct 27 16:39:10 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
 15697  8525 Z    Mon Oct 26 08:14:29 2026     <defunct>
 20353  8525 S    Wed Oct 28 19:06:05 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
 28105  8525 S    Thu Oct 29 10:14:00 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
 38001  8525 Z    Wed Oct 28 19:46:39 2026     <defunct>
 44482  8525 Z    Tue Oct 27 00:53:55 2026     <defunct>
 45074  8525 Z    Wed Oct 28 16:16:35 2026     <defunct>
 46152  8525 Z    Tue Oct 27 10:07:28 2026     <defunct>
 53422  8525 S    Tue Oct 27 02:30:15 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
 54680  8525 Z    Wed Oct 28 00:14:19 2026     <defunct>
 58567  8525 Z    Thu Oct 29 03:22:58 2026     <defunct>
 63623  8525 Z    Thu Oct 29 04:22:32 2026     <defunct>
 67758  8525 Z    Mon Oct 26 17:43:31 2026     <defunct>
 75418  8525 S    Wed Oct 28 17:03:45 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
 80894  8525 Z    Wed Oct 28 11:04:22 2026     <defunct>
 85579  8525 S    Thu Oct 29 14:10:30 2026     /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -w 8525
 96202  8525 S    Thu Oct 29 14:23:36 2026     /Users/<user>/.cache/magpie/bun/1.4.4/magpie-bun run /Users/<user>/.cache/magpie/plugin-host/host-6eabac8b763e.js
```

Every zombie's start time lines up with a live `caffeinate` start time (same hour, roughly the same pattern), so the count grows one-for-one with keep-awake sessions: 12 zombies in ~3 days.

The cost today is negligible (RSS 0, no fd), but the count never drops until magpie exits, and on a long-running setup it accumulates indefinitely.

### Why, as far as I can tell

`caffeinate` is a normal helper the way the probe helpers are: once it exits, someone needs to call `Wait()` on its `exec.Cmd` to reap it. On the evidence here, whatever goroutine starts `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` either drops the `Cmd` when the wake session ends or only calls `Wait()` on one of several paths. This looks like the same family of problem as #3285 (plugin host left a zombie after `syscall.Exec`), but the trigger here is the keep-awake helper on macOS, not the plugin host or reexec, and it reproduces without any update or restart.

### Suggested fix

Wherever the wake session is torn down, also `Wait()` the `caffeinate` `Cmd` — same discipline the probes use. If the Cmd is handed off between goroutines, keeping a single owner that does `cmd.Wait()` in a defer when the session ends would cover it.

### Environment

- magpie 0.1.1985, macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- `magpie serve --web=127.0.0.1:3430` (menu-bar app, launched from `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.yetone.magpie.serve.plist`)
- Bun 1.4.4, go1.26.8
- Not running under systemd (macOS launchd); no reexec involved during the observation window

```
   314       9 Z    magpie-bun
  2167       9 Z    magpie-bun
  2967       9 Z    magpie-bun
  ...                                   (22 in all)
231388       9 Sl   magpie-bun          <- the host of the image now running

$ ps -eo stat,comm | grep -c Z
22
$ awk '/magpie gateway on/{n++} END{print n}' ~/.local/share/magpie/web.log
23
```

23 images have run under that one PID and 22 Bun hosts are `<defunct>`: exactly one per reexec, none missed, none duplicated. Each zombie's start time is the host that was up when the previous image was replaced — 21:33:47 → reexec 21:59, 22:00:47 → 22:19, 22:19:55 → 23:01, 23:02:05 → 23:09, 02:10:38 → 05:10 — and each new image wrote a new `plugin-host/host-<hash>.js` (five of those on disk).

Two things that may help whoever fixes it:

`/proc/<pid>/exe` is the binary now on disk (`md5sum` equal to `.local/bin/magpie`, mtime 23:29) while the process started two days earlier, which is what pins this on the in-place exec rather than on a handover.

After the exec the parent holds no pipes at all — `/proc/9/fd` has exactly three, the live host's stdin/stdout/stderr — because they are all `O_CLOEXEC` and the exec closed them. That is also why the old host is not stuck: it gets stdin EOF and exits. There is just no `wait4` left to take it, since the only one was `host.read()`'s `cmd.Wait()` in the image that was replaced.

And since a reexec is the one place magpie puts a new image in its own PID, the ending should probably be the general one: anything else that outlives an exec is the same `<defunct>` under the same PID afterwards (pii's helper, whatever `magpie awake` holds — #4188's `caffeinate` is that shape too, though it may not be this path). The `plugin.Settle` plus wait-for-reap in skygunner's comment above is the shape I would expect; it is not in `59fdab0af` yet.

issue.title: Web 升级重启卡死：host.stop 提前返回，EndHosts 等待存活的插件进程

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Description

在 macOS 的 `magpie serve --web=0.0.0.0:3430` 服务中，通过 Web 页面点击升级重启后，Web 的 3430 监听消失，但旧 Magpie 进程和它的 Bun 子进程继续存活；3425 网关仍监听，插件供应商持续返回 `magpie is restarting; the plugins are back in a moment`，直到手动执行 `magpie daemon restart` 才恢复。

源码中存在一个与现场高度吻合、可以独立确定性复现的停止竞态：**`host.stop()` 把表示传输失效的 `h.dead` 当作子进程已经退出，提前返回并跳过 Kill；`EndHosts()` 随后仍无限等待真正的子进程退出，导致 Web 的 reexec 永远执行不到。**

## Steps to Reproduce

现场操作路径如下，并非声明每次点击都会触发：

1. 通过 launchd 运行 `magpie serve --web=0.0.0.0:3430`，有插件供应商请求在运行。
2. 在 Web 页面点击升级重启。
3. 若插件 stdin 关闭时仍有写入，且 Bun 中仍有未结束的任务，可能命中下述停止竞态：Web 端口关闭、旧进程不退出，插件一直处于 restarting。

现场只观察到一次事故，未在共享服务上再次点击升级来复现；下面附有不连接 Magpie、不读取配置、不占用服务端口的独立 Go 复现，强制构造对应的时序。

## Expected Behavior

Web 更新重启应在有界时间内结束旧插件 host，然后执行新版本；3430 恢复监听，插件恢复服务。管道关闭或 RPC host 失效，不应被当作 OS 子进程已经结束。

## Actual Behavior

- 旧版本 0.1.2889 的进程一直存活；磁盘上的程序已是 0.1.2910。
- Web 3430 不再监听，而网关 3425 仍监听。
- GLM 插件请求持续返回 restarting；Codex 等内置供应商仍能接受请求。
- 故障期间保存的进程快照显示旧 Magpie PID 27974 及其 Bun 子进程 PID 45100 均存活。
- 17:03 手动 `magpie daemon restart` 后，进程切换到 0.1.2910，Web 监听、原生登录、登录后首页和前端脚本均恢复。

## Environment

- OS: macOS，Darwin 25.6.0，arm64。
- 启动方式：用户级 launchd 服务，`magpie serve --web=0.0.0.0:3430`。
- 事故时实际运行版本：0.1.2889；磁盘版本和恢复后版本：0.1.2910。
- 插件运行时：magpie-bun 1.4.4；受影响的已观察路由包括 zcode/GLM-5.3 和 zcode/GLM-5.3-Flash。
- 截至提报前检查，最新发布版为 **v0.1.2922**（2026-11-04 09:30:15 UTC）；`main` 为 `8ac5f98e2af56fc3bf934a7e761a43f58ab7f185`。

## Screenshots/Logs

以下为 2026-11-04 本地时间 UTC+08:00，省略账号和所有登录链接参数：

```text
16:36:34 gateway: claude's call to zcode/GLM-5.3 on zcode failed: 200 after 27.695s: ZCode: connection lost mid-reply (writing to the plugin host: write |1: file already closed)
16:37:07 gateway: claude's call to zcode/GLM-5.3-Flash on zcode failed: 502 after 34.912s: magpie is restarting; the plugins are back in a moment
16:37:08 gateway: claude's call to zcode/GLM-5.3 on zcode failed: 502 after 34.281s: magpie is restarting; the plugins are back in a moment
16:57:06 gateway: claude's call to zcode/GLM-5.3 on zcode failed: 502 after 33.347s: magpie is restarting; the plugins are back in a moment
```

16:50 的进程/监听快照仍显示：

```text
PID    PPID   STARTED             PROCESS
27974     1   2026-11-04 10:31:34  magpie
45100 27974   2026-11-04 15:34:39  magpie-bun

magpie 27974: *:3425 LISTEN
magpie 27974: 127.0.0.1:57929 LISTEN
(no 3430 listener)
```

## Additional Context

### 源码中的失败链

以下链接固定在最新发布版 v0.1.2922，避免开发分支变化：

1. [`Web.Wait()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2922/internal/gui/web.go#L134-L149) 先 `w.srv.Close()`，然后 `plugin.EndHosts()`，最后才 `update.Reexec(...)`。
2. [`EndHosts()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2922/internal/plugin/host.go#L546-L564) 设置 `live.ended = true`，阻止新的插件 host 启动；对每个旧 host 调用 `h.stop(); h.wait()`，最后 `wg.Wait()`。这里没有整体等待上限。
3. [`host.stop()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2922/internal/plugin/host.go#L907-L929) 先关闭 `h.in`；如果此时 `h.dead` 关闭，立刻返回，跳过后面的 `h.cmd.Process.Kill()`。
4. [`writerLoop()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2922/internal/plugin/host.go#L1503-L1529) 写入已关闭的 stdin 时调用 `h.fail(...)`；[`fail()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2922/internal/plugin/host.go#L1536-L1567) 会关闭 `h.dead`，**这时子进程可以仍然存活**。
5. [`proc.Output.Start()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2922/internal/proc/output.go#L70-L104) 的 wait 要等 OS 子进程实际结束；输出管道的 grace period 在 `cmd.Wait()` 返回后才开始，不能限制一个仍存活的子进程。

因此有如下时序：

```text
Web.Wait: close Web -> EndHosts
EndHosts: live.ended=true
stop:     close stdin
writer:   write fails -> fail -> close(h.dead)
stop:     sees h.dead -> returns without killing child
EndHosts: h.wait() / wg.Wait() waits for the still-live child indefinitely
Web.Wait: never reaches Reexec
```

Bun host 关闭 stdin 后会等 pending 工作清零再退出；本来 `stopWait`/Kill 应负责约束这个等待，但上述时序跳过了 Kill。旧父进程不退出，launchd 也无法靠进程退出触发恢复。

已逐函数核对：`EndHosts`、`host.stop`、`host.wait`、`writerLoop`、`host.fail` 在 v0.1.2889、v0.1.2910、v0.1.2922 和上述 main 提交中相同；`web.go` 与 `proc/output.go` 的相关实现也相同。**这属于源码核查，并未把本机升级到 v0.1.2922 做线上更新复现。**

### 独立验证及结论边界

下方测试中的 `host.stop()` 与事故版本源码逐字相同，也与 v0.1.2922 相同。用一个忽略 stdin 的临时 `/bin/sleep` 子进程代表仍有 pending 工作的 host；在 stdin 关闭后触发写入错误，并模拟 `h.fail` 关闭 `h.dead`。测试确认停止函数返回后子进程仍活着，随后的实际 `Wait` 仍阻塞。测试结束会 kill 并回收自己的临时子进程。

```text
STOP_METHOD_EXACT_MATCH True
=== RUN   TestOriginalStopLeavesLiveChildAfterPipeFailure
REPRODUCED: stop_returned_after=102.183625ms child_alive=true subsequent_wait_blocked=true writer_error="write |1: file already closed"
--- PASS: TestOriginalStopLeavesLiveChildAfterPipeFailure (0.11s)
```

`PASS` 表示成功验证缺陷条件，**不是修复已经通过**。现场没有保留挂住进程的 goroutine dump，因此事故的具体阻塞栈仍是基于日志、父子进程存活情况和源码时序的高度吻合推断；停止函数将传输失效混同于进程退出的问题则由隔离实验直接验证。

建议回归覆盖“host 已失效但子进程仍活着”的停止场景，并按实际进程退出状态实施有界等待/终止，而非仅依赖 RPC 的 `h.dead`。

相关但不同的问题：#3285 讨论 reexec 遗留僵尸子进程；#2362 / #4983 讨论桌面应用已退出后没有重新拉起。这里是浏览器/serve 的 reexec **之前**旧父子进程仍存活、Web 已关闭。

<details>
<summary>完整独立 Go 复现（保存为 stop_test.go）</summary>

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local GO111MODULE=off go test -count=1 -timeout 8s -v stop_test.go
```

```go
package restartproof

import (
	"errors"
	"io"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// Minimal host fields used by the reviewed stop method. No Magpie code,
// configuration, ports, credentials, or running service is loaded here.
type host struct {
	in       io.WriteCloser
	dead     chan struct{}
	renewing atomic.Int32
	cmd      *exec.Cmd
}

var (
	stopWait     = 2 * time.Second
	stopRenewing = 15 * time.Second
)

// Copied verbatim from internal/plugin/host.go:906-928 at v0.1.2889.
func (h *host) stop() {
	h.in.Close()
	start := time.Now()
	wait := time.NewTimer(stopWait)
	defer wait.Stop()
	select {
	case <-h.dead:
		return
	case <-wait.C:
	}
	tick := time.NewTicker(20 * time.Millisecond)
	defer tick.Stop()
	for h.renewing.Load() > 0 && time.Since(start) < stopRenewing {
		select {
		case <-h.dead:
			return
		case <-tick.C:
		}
	}
	if h.cmd.Process != nil {
		h.cmd.Process.Kill()
	}
}

// Make a write attempt happen strictly after stop closes the pipe.
type closeNotifyingPipe struct {
	io.WriteCloser
	closed chan struct{}
	once   sync.Once
}

func (p *closeNotifyingPipe) Close() error {
	err := p.WriteCloser.Close()
	p.once.Do(func() { close(p.closed) })
	return err
}

func TestOriginalStopLeavesLiveChildAfterPipeFailure(t *testing.T) {
	// This child deliberately does not read stdin, standing for a host
	// with background work still keeping its event loop alive after EOF.
	cmd := exec.Command("/bin/sleep", "30")
	stdin, err := cmd.StdinPipe()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	waited := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { waited <- cmd.Wait() }()
	defer func() {
		_ = cmd.Process.Kill()
		select {
		case <-waited:
		case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
			t.Error("test child did not finish during cleanup")
		}
	}()

	pipe := &closeNotifyingPipe{WriteCloser: stdin, closed: make(chan struct{})}
	h := &host{cmd: cmd, in: pipe, dead: make(chan struct{})}
	writerError := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		<-pipe.closed
		_, err := stdin.Write([]byte("request\n"))
		writerError <- err
		// host.writerLoop calls h.fail on this error; h.fail closes dead
		// independently of whether the child process has exited.
		if err != nil {
			close(h.dead)
		}
	}()

	stopped := make(chan struct{})
	started := time.Now()
	go func() {
		h.stop()
		close(stopped)
	}()
	select {
	case <-stopped:
	case <-time.After(3 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("stop did not return")
	}
	writeErr := <-writerError
	if !errors.Is(writeErr, os.ErrClosed) {
		t.Fatalf("expected the observed closed-pipe error, got %v", writeErr)
	}
	if err := cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.Signal(0)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected the child to remain alive, got %v", err)
	}
	select {
	case err := <-waited:
		t.Fatalf("expected EndHosts' subsequent wait to remain blocked, got %v", err)
	case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
	}
	t.Logf("REPRODUCED: stop_returned_after=%s child_alive=true subsequent_wait_blocked=true writer_error=%q", time.Since(started), writeErr)
}
```

</details>

timeline.body: Thank you for the second machine and the forensics — the `O_CLOEXEC` reading (the exec closes every pipe, so the old host dies of stdin EOF with no `wait4` left to reap it) is exactly the mechanism the fix runs on: [fix/reexec-plugin-host](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/reexec-plugin-host) (`863a1e72`) drains the gateway, then `plugin.Settle`, then waits for the reaping before the reexec, covering both the clean and the forced-kill exit. Still awaiting pickup — nothing in `59fdab0af` takes it, as you found. Your broader point is noted: anything else that outlives the exec under the same PID is the same `<defunct>` shape afterwards; the branch scopes itself to the reexec path for now.

Follow-up: the reexec plugin-host fix has now landed upstream as f4c664a09ca0e2dcdab3d41290e10ba440a1367f: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/f4c664a09ca0e2dcdab3d41290e10ba440a1367f . On main at b1e8eb15, Web.Wait calls plugin.EndHosts immediately before update.Reexec; EndHosts prevents new hosts, stops live and retiring hosts, and waits for each child to be reaped. This supersedes my earlier "still awaiting pickup" status for this plugin-host path.

I reran TestEndHostsLeavesNoChild on Linux at that baseline with the related web/plugin tests: it passed. I did not perform a downloaded-update reexec against a deployed service, and this does not establish that unrelated helper processes in #4188 are fixed.

The separate SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful-drain port discussed in #1258 is refreshed on the same baseline in https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/1258-web-shutdown-current (e094d775c13ac24014d0227365d00df9e7c487b6, with the original author's co-author credit). It preserves ignored signals and SIGHUP behavior, covers web and serve --web, drains held real HTTP requests before exit, and suppresses an update restart on cancellation. Twelve Linux subprocess scenarios, the ignored-signal disposition check, race, related tests, vet and nogui build passed. This branch uses upstream's EndHosts rather than carrying a second implementation. Native Windows/macOS and a real update download were not exercised. The upstream PR has not been modified.

issue.title: plugin host: the heavy-host guard samples once a minute from ten minutes of uptime, so a host that grows 1 GB in two seconds is OOM-killed before it ever runs

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

On a 2 GB host the plugin host (`bun`) was being killed by the kernel OOM killer every 1–2 minutes. Each kill took down every in-flight request on every plugin provider:

```
gateway: <caller>'s call to group/auto on <provider> failed: 200 after 25.221s: <Provider>: connection lost mid-reply (the plugin host quit: signal: killed)
```

`dmesg` shows the victim is always `(bun)`, and the kill is a **global** OOM — whichever process faults next invokes the killer, and the kernel then picks the largest task:

```
Out of memory: Killed process 14221 (bun) total-vm:8596600kB, anon-rss:1272316kB, ... UID:65532
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,...,global_oom,task_memcg=/services,task=bun,pid=14221,uid=65532
```

The invoking process varies run to run (`containerd`, `sing-box`, `procd`, `adb`, `logd`, `smbd-cleanupd`, `bun`, and `magpie-native` once) — every one of them ends with a `(bun)` victim, so the dying host is a second-order effect of the box running out of memory, not one caller's fault.

Over one day (2026-11-12): **930** host starts and **70** client-visible `signal: killed` failures. Across the whole log (1422 host starts over six days) there are **zero** `host holds ...` lines — the guard never fired once.

## The guard exists, but cannot fire here

`internal/plugin/host.go`:

```go
// heavyMB is how much memory a host may hold before it is replaced:
// past it, and still past it after a full collection, the host says so
// ("heavy") and a new host takes the calls made from then on while the
// old one finishes its own (recycle).
var (
	heavyMB    = 512
	heavyAfter = 10 * time.Minute
	heavyEvery = time.Minute
)
```

and `watchHeavy` in the host script:

```js
const timer = setInterval(() => {
  if (process.uptime() * 1000 < after || rss() <= mb) return
  Bun.gc(true)
  const held = rss()
  if (held <= mb) return
  clearInterval(timer)
  send({ event: "heavy", count: Math.round(held) })
}, every)
```

Two things make it unreachable for this failure mode:

1. **It starts sampling only after `heavyAfter` = 10 minutes of uptime.** The hosts in this incident lived ~1–2 minutes, so the guard never sampled once. 
2. **Even for a long-lived host, a 2-second ramp slips between two 60-second samples.** Measured at 50 ms resolution, a host went from 120 MB to 624 MB in about two seconds (25–30 MB per sample), then the kernel ended it. A once-a-minute check cannot see a burst that fast.

So the only thing that bounded the host was the OOM killer — which bounds it by killing the process and, with it, every other plugin provider's in-flight request.

## Measured without the guard

Sampling `/proc/<pid>/status` `VmRSS` every 50 ms while the host served its normal traffic:

```
120 MB steady for ~100 s
201 231 256 279 304 329 357 382 412 442 470 498 526 553 576 598 624 MB   (each step 50 ms apart)
→ killed
```

`dmesg` tasks tables put the victim's `anon-rss` at 712–807 MB in the ordinary case, and 1.18–1.30 GB after a 1 GB zram device was added. Idle baseline is 100–130 MB, `VmHWM` 130–200 MB — so it is a burst, not a slow leak.

## What I would ask for

Any of these would turn a crash into a bounded failure:

1. **Sample early and often for the first minutes.** A host can die within a minute of starting; today's `heavyAfter` (10 min) means the whole first ten minutes of a host's life are unguarded. Something like `min(heavyEvery, ...)` decreasing over time, or simply `heavyAfter = 0` with a short first interval.
2. **Or bound it from outside the JS heap** — the guard reads `process.memoryUsage().rss` from inside the same process, so it competes with the allocation it is watching. A parent-side watchdog (read the child's RSS from `/proc`, or a cgroup/rlimit on the child) would see the burst even when the JS thread is busy allocating.
3. **Name the allocator.** When the host dies, the log says `the plugin host quit: signal: killed` with no indication of which plugin's call was in flight or how much it held. In this incident the client-visible provider name was misleading — it named whichever request happened to be in flight, and users reasonably concluded that plugin was at fault.

## Cause of this particular burst (for context, not a magpie bug)

A community plugin read a whole routing trace file into memory — `gunzipSync(readFileSync(path))` on a 47.6 MB `.jsonl.gz` that decompressed to 520 MB, plus a `text.split("\n")` copy on top. Reported separately against that plugin. The point here is the host-side response: the burst was 2 seconds long and the guard samples every 60 seconds from minute 10.

Related: #4916 (one plugin's blocking call stalls every plugin; name it and isolate it), #5699 (host killed by the 32 MB wire-line limit), #3285 (old Bun host left a zombie after an auto-update restart).

issue.title: plugin host: thousands of live magpie-bun processes accumulate until the container hits pids.max; every request then 502s on fork/exec EAGAIN (0.1.2421, docker)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

magpie `0.1.2421` (linux/arm64, local docker build) running as `magpie web --addr 0.0.0.0:3430 --no-open`, container `pids` limit 4096. After days of uptime the container's `pids.current` reached **4091/4096** and every `fork`/`exec` inside it — a plain `sh` included — failed:

```
$ docker exec magpie-magpie-1 sh -c 'echo hi'
sh: 0: Cannot fork
```

From the client's side every Claude Code request through the gateway returned:

```
502 {"error":{"message":"Claude Code: fork/exec /config/cache/magpie/claude-code/2.1.310/claude: resource temporarily unavailable","type":"api_error"},"type":"error"}
```

`pgrep -u 65532 -c` counted **4063 processes** for the container user; essentially all of them were `magpie-bun`, each with a single task under `/proc/<pid>/task`, state `S` (sleeping) — **live processes, not `<defunct>` zombies**. `etimes` ranged from fresh up to ~736,000s (≈8.5 days) with a second large batch around ~255,000s, so they had been accumulating for over a week, not in one burst.

A `docker restart` dropped `pids.current` to 19 and the gateway immediately served again — 200 on `/v1/magpie/quotas/cards`, Claude Code requests flowing within a minute.

## What the log says

- **106 `Bun has crashed` blocks** in the container log, all the same shape — `panic(main thread): abort() called` ~75ms after start, `Peak: ~1.1 GB`:

  ```
  Args: "/config/cache/magpie/bun/1.4.2/magpie-bun" "run" "/config/cache/magpie/plugin-host/host-57e4026712e7.js"
  panic(main thread): abort() called
  oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
  ```

- Repeated failed (re)starts, minutes apart:

  ```
  plugin check-in: SunflowersLwtech: starting plugins: the plugin host quit: signal: aborted (core dumped)
  listing the plugins' models again: starting plugins: the plugin host quit: signal: aborted (core dumped) (the last lists stay)
  starting plugins: context deadline exceeded
  ```

- `plugins: Bun 1.4.4 set aside, the plugin host died on it` — it had already tried Bun 1.4.4 and fallen back to the bundled 1.4.2.

So a plugin (re)start leaves a `magpie-bun` process behind — alive, sleeping, never reaped — while the next check-in/refresh spawns another, and the crash loop keeps producing more. Once the count reaches `pids.max`, the failure mode is total: not just the plugin host but **every** `exec` in the container fails, so even model requests that don't need a plugin return 502.

## How this differs from the open issues I found

- **#3285** (auto-update leaves the old Bun host a `<defunct>` zombie): ours are *live* processes that count toward the pids limit and hold memory; a zombie would not.
- **#5402** (a plugin host ended leaves the processes the plugin started): the leaked processes here are the hosts themselves (`magpie-bun run .../plugin-host/host-*.js`), not a plugin's own children.
- **#3890** (shared stream limit → local 502s): same user-visible 502 surface, different cause — ours persists until restart, with no request concurrency at all.

## Version note

This build predates the host-lifecycle fixes already on `main` — the wait/reap work and #3285 in v0.1.2840, #5402 in v0.1.3063, #4678 in v0.1.3074, the over-512-MiB host replacement in v0.1.3330. We're upgrading the deployment and will watch whether live hosts still accumulate on a current version; filing because the observed mode (live `magpie-bun` accumulation to `pids` exhaustion → `fork/exec` EAGAIN → all requests 502) does not match an existing open issue, and because the Bun abort loop means whatever the start path leaves behind keeps growing.

Happy to pull `/proc` maps/cmdlines, core-dump artifacts, or more of the container log while this fresh instance is still clean — or to re-run the same counts after the upgrade.

issue.title: kill(pid, 0) takes a zombie for a live process: 18 lock/liveness checks across 15 packages

repository.name: plugins
repository.description: Community-maintained OpenCode provider plugins for coding-plan subscriptions (work in OpenCode and magpie)

issue.body:
`process.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds on a zombie (an exited process its parent hasn't reaped), so every helper below takes an exited process for a live one while it stays `<defunct>`.

Where that lasts:
- magpie as a container's PID 1 adopts every orphan. `magpie serve` reaps them (382c8c0bd, ~10s after exit); `magpie web`, the Docker docs' command, didn't, which left a third-party plugin's AI Studio process a zombie for good and blocked its restarts (swang20201 on X; magpie-gemini-web PR BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web#59, magpie fix for `web` landing separately).
- yetone/magpie#3285: after an auto-update's `syscall.Exec` the old Bun host stays a `<defunct>` child of magpie on Linux, on any machine. A lock file that names that host's pid then looks held forever.

Sites on main (4a64252b), each a lock owner or "is it still running" check:

| Package | Site | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agent-console | `index.mjs:74`, `daemon/src/util/proc.ts:9` | pidAlive |
| agent-office | `lib/scan.mjs:300`, `lib/jump.mjs:80` | pidAlive |
| agy-cli | `index.mjs` (owner.pid check near 1996) | lock owner |
| astudio | `browser.mjs:57` | lock owner |
| gcp-ai | `lib/lock.mjs:20` | lock owner (falls back to age) |
| goanyapi | `src/auth.ts:122` | lock owner (age too) |
| kimi-desktop | `adapter.mjs:273` | lock owner |
| mclaw | `browser.mjs:66` | lock owner |
| nanobot | `runtime.mjs:57`, `bridge.mjs:210` | lock owner (`writer_locked`) |
| nowledge-mem-agent | `lib/files.mjs:33` | lock owner |
| page-harnessweight | `harnessweight.hooks.mjs:144` | lock owner |
| reasonix-desktop | `bridge.mjs:66` | lock owner |
| respire-memory | `lock.mjs:8` | lock owner |
| search1api | `src/auth.ts:122` | lock owner (age too) |
| window-warmup | `src/store.ts:288` | pidAlive |

Fix (as in magpie-gemini-web's `lib/proc.mjs`): after `kill(pid, 0)` succeeds (or EPERM), read `/proc/<pid>/stat` and take the state after the last `)`; `Z` or `X` means exited. No readable `/proc` entry (macOS, Windows) leaves the answer as it is. One shared helper beats 18 copies; a test can point it at a fake `/proc` tree with a `Z` state, and on Linux a real zombie comes from `sh -c 'sleep 0 & echo $!; exec sleep 30'`.

The lasting cases are better closed on the magpie side too (reaping under `web`, and #3285), so this is the plugins' half.
